question: Which of the following was discovered by Henri Becquerel?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Radioactivity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Radioactivity**

 
 
• The spontaneous emission of energy and particles from the nucleus of an unstable atom.
 
• Types of Radiation: Alpha particles, beta particles, gamma rays, and neutrons.
 
• Wavelength: Not applicable, as radioactivity is not a form of electromagnetic radiation.
 
• Sources: Naturally occurring radioactive elements like uranium and radium, as well as man-made sources like nuclear reactors and medical equipment.
 
• Effects: Can be harmful to living organisms, causing damage to cells and DNA. However, radioactivity also has beneficial applications in medicine, industry, and research.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ultraviolet (UV) Light**

 
 
• Definition: A type of electromagnetic radiation with wavelengths shorter than visible light but longer than X-rays.
 
• Wavelength: 10-400 nanometers (nm).
 
• Sources: The sun, artificial sources like tanning beds and black lights.
 
• Effects: Can cause sunburn, premature aging, and skin cancer. However, UV light also plays a crucial role in the production of vitamin D in the human body.
 
• Types: UV-A, UV-B, and UV-C, with UV-B being the most harmful type.
 
 
 
• **Infrared (IR) Radiation**
 
 
• A type of electromagnetic radiation with wavelengths longer than visible light but shorter than microwaves.
 
• Wavelength: 700 nanometers (nm) to 1 millimeter (mm).
 
• Heat sources like the sun, fire, and hot objects.
 
• Primarily felt as heat. It has various applications, including thermal imaging, remote controls, and medical treatments.
 
• Types: Near-infrared, mid-infrared, and far-infrared, each with different wavelengths and applications.
 
 
 
• **X-Rays**
 
 
• A type of high-energy electromagnetic radiation with wavelengths shorter than ultraviolet light.
 
• Wavelength: 0.01 to 10 nanometers (nm).
 
• X-ray tubes, medical imaging equipment, and cosmic rays.
 
• Can penetrate many materials, including human tissue, making them useful for medical imaging. However, excessive exposure can be harmful, leading to cell damage and an increased risk of cancer.
 
• Medical imaging (X-rays, CT scans), security screening, and industrial applications.
